facts.statement: Amygdalodon is an extinct genus of basal sauropod known for its almond-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Amygdalodon (; "almond tooth" for its almond shaped teeth) is an extinct genus of basal sauropod from the Early Jurassic of Argentina.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon was estimated to be 12 meters long and 4 meters tall.
facts.quote: Amygdalodon is estimated to have been 12 m long and 4 m tall.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon was a quadrupedal dinosaur with an estimated weight of over 5 tonnes.
facts.quote: This quadrupedal dinosaur had an estimated weight of over 5 t.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon reached a length of 15 meters and a height of 4 meters, weighing more than several tonnes.
facts.quote: llegó a medir 15 metros de largo y 4 de alto y a pesar más de toneladas.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon had laterally compressed teeth that were slightly curved inward, giving the genus its name.
facts.quote: Tenía dientes en forma de almendra, de donde proviene su nombre, están comprimidos lateralmente y ligeramente curvados hacia adentro.

facts.statement: The teeth of Amygdalodon were spatulate in shape and lacked denticles on their crowns.
facts.quote: La morfología de los dientes, que se caracterizan por su forma espatulada y ausencia de dentículos en sus coronas.

facts.statement: The holotype of Amygdalodon, discovered in 1936, includes vertebrae, ribs, teeth, a partial pelvis, and a shoulder blade.
facts.quote: The holotype (MLP 46-VIII-21-1) consists of some vertebrae, ribs, four complete and three partial teeth, and a partial pelvis and shoulder-blade, of which was discovered in 1936.

facts.statement: The type species Amygdalodon patagonicus was described by Cabrera in Argentina in 1947.
facts.quote: The type species, Amygdalodon patagonicus, was described by Cabrera in Argentina in 1947.

facts.statement: The fossils were donated to the Museo de La Plata and cataloged as number 46-VIII-21-1.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por Cabrera en 1947, los fósiles se catalogan Núm. 46-VIII-21-1 del Departamento de Paleozoología, Vertebrados, del Museo de La Plata y fueron donados por la Dirección General de Yacimientos Petrolíferos Fiscales.

facts.statement: Fossils of Amygdalodon have been found in the Toarcian-aged Cerro Carnerero Formation, dating to about 180-172 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of Amygdalodon have been found in the Toarcian-aged Cerro Carnerero Formation (about 180-172 million years ago).

facts.statement: Amygdalodon lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 180 to 171 million years ago, in what is now Argentina.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 180 a 171 millones de años, desde el Toarciense hasta el Aaleniense, en lo que hoy es Argentina.

facts.statement: Remains of Amygdalodon were found in Chubut Province, east of the Sierra de Pampa de Agnía locality in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en la Provincia del Chubut, al este de la localidad de Sierra de Pampa de Agnía, en Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: Rauhut (2003) classified Amygdalodon as Eusauropoda incertae sedis based on the type material.
facts.quote: Rauhut (2003) placed Amygdalodon as Eusauropoda incertae sedis based on examination of the type material.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis by Carballido et al. (2010) recovered Amygdalodon as a non-eusauropod sauropod.
facts.quote: Later, a cladistic analysis conducted by Carballido et al. (2010) recovered the genus as a non-eusauropod sauropod.

facts.statement: Holwerda and Pol (2018) recovered Amygdalodon as the sister taxon to Isanosaurus.
facts.quote: Holwerda and Pol (2018) concurred, recovering Amygdalodon as sister to Isanosaurus.

facts.statement: Pol and colleagues (2022) supported a basal sauropod classification for Amygdalodon, noting early signs of dental modification for bulk feeding but lacking derived vertebral features.
facts.quote: A basal sauropod classification for Amygdalodon was supported by Pol and colleagues in 2022, with it showing the first signs of dental modification for bulk feeding that is retained in later sauropods, but it does not have the vertebral features found in more derived sauropods.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon is considered a Cetiosauridae due to specific vertebral features with only simple lateral depressions.
facts.quote: Es considerado un Cetiosauridae debido a particularidades en las vértebras que solo poseen depresiones laterales simples.

facts.statement: Based on phylogenetic analysis, Amygdalodon is interpreted as a non-eusauropod sauropod.
facts.quote: En base al análisis filogenético realizado, es interpretado como un saurópodo no-eusaurópodo.

facts.statement: Due to the fragmentary nature of the available material, alternative positions placing Amygdalodon within Eusauropoda exist.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, debido a lo fragmentario del material disponible, posiciones alternativas que ubican a Amygdalodon dentro de Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the material represents very basal non-neosauropod eusauropods.
facts.quote: Todo el material que originalmente se refería a esta especie representa no-neosaurópodos eusaurópodos muy basales.

facts.statement: Derived dental characters in Amygdalodon, such as crown-to-crown occlusion and buccal and lingual grooves, suggest some traits previously thought unique to Eusauropoda appeared earlier in sauropod evolution.
facts.quote: La presencia de caracteres dentales derivados presentes en los dientes de este taxón, como por ejemplo la presencia de oclusión corona-corona o la presencia de surcos bucales y linguales, muestra que algunos caracteres previamente interpretados como vistos solamente en Eusauropoda habrían aparecido más temprano en la evolución de los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon is one of the few Jurassic dinosaurs known from South America.
facts.quote: Very little is known about it, but it is one of the few Jurassic dinosaurs from South America found thus far.

facts.statement: Amygdalodon is the only evidence in South America for a probable early Middle Jurassic basal eusauropod, suggesting global dispersal.
facts.quote: Amygdalodon es la única evidencia en América del Sur para un probable saurópodo eusaurópodo basal temprano a principios del Jurásico Medio mostrando dispersión mundial.
